sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: This document introduces the PUSH integration services available in JINT for covered Jaggaer One modules.

Push services have been introduced to support real-time and near real-time process where it is required to send data from Jaggaer One to an external system and therefore an integration solution based on “CALL-ME” web-services (either REST or SOAP) based on a the PULL logic was not well-fitting since it requires the client component to “call” the web-services very frequently.

While in case of “call-me” services supporting the PULL logic, regardless of the data-flow direction, the JINT exposes a web-service to be invoked by a client component running at customer or partner side, in case of “push” services it is JINT that sends a message to the server component exposed by the partner/customer when an event occurs in Jaggaer One.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In order to implement a “push” based integration the following pre-requisites need to be checked
1. The required JINT dataflow must support the “push” based communication (please refer to the JINT Web Services Library and Activation request document)
2. The customer/partner must be able to expose a service to receive the message sent by the JINT and in the JINT format (see 2.3-Message format) and provide back a response in a timely manner
3. The service must run on an URL exposed on the internet via HTTPS

The message exchange between Jaggaer One platform and the external system (via the JINT) can be synchronous or asynchronous. This depends mainly on the functional features available on the related JaggaerOne module and the required processes to be executed on the external system to provide a feedback (if they can be executed in real time or not).

sections.title: Synchronous data exchange
paragraphs: As soon as an event is generated by Jaggaer One (e.g. a purchase order is approved in the workflow and an “export” robot is configured as next step) the JINT prepares the message and sends it to the configured endpoint.
The external system processes it immediately and provide as response the outcome of the process (e.g. if the purchase order is valid for the ERP).
JaggaerOne platform receives the response and operates accordingly based on available features and configuration.
Below diagram representing the synchronous exchange

sections.title: Asynchronous data exchange
paragraphs: When event is generated by Jaggaer One (e.g. a purchase order is approved in the workflow and a “validate” robot is configured as next step) the JINT prepares the message and sends it to the configured endpoint.
The external system acknowledges JINT it received the message and processes it on a later stage.

Once the message has been processed the external system will call already available “call-me” web-services to inform Jaggaer One about the outcome of the process (e.g. if the purchase order is valid for the ERP).
When the external system processes the message, it could be required as well to consume other “call-me” web-services exposed by JINT to get additional data and/or files.
The web-service call will be processed according to the specific features available on involved the Jaggaer One module and related configuration
Below diagram representing the synchronous exchange

To secure the communication between JINT and the external system is based on HTTPs only then the channel is encrypted
The following additional security measures can be applied to allow the external system to authenticate the JINT
1. HTTP Basic [segreto]: each HTTP message pushed by JINT to the external system contains username/password defined during the setup of the integration
2. Signed JWT: each HTTP message pushed by JINT to the external system contains a bearer token representing a signed JWT
3. SSL mutual authentication (not yet available): the external system during the SSL handshake requires JINT to provide a client certificate to prove its identity
To enable and configure a push service it is necessary to create a JINT side configuration.
A push configuration contains information like:
the ObjectType (PO, PR, Invoice, Receipt or J1Supplier)
the operation type (for example export or validate)
authentication data like the login and the password
the format type (it is possible to choose between 3 types of format: xml, json or soap)
For the same event (a couple of customer-ObjectType) there can be multiple configurations: one configuration for each type of operation type requested.
